# Methods reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_reference.py from the engine registry. Do not edit. -->

Every method is available with the same id and inputs from Python (`fm.run`),
the CLI (`fairmark run`), MCP and function calling
(tool name `fairmark_<id with underscores>`).
Decimals may be passed as JSON numbers or strings and are returned as strings.

## `dates.year_fraction`

**Year fraction (day count)** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_dates_year_fraction`

Fraction of a year between two dates under an ISDA 2006 day-count convention: Actual/365 Fixed, Actual/360, Actual/Actual ISDA, 30/360, 30E/360.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `start` | string | yes |  | Start date (ISO 8601). |
| `end` | string | yes |  | End date (ISO 8601), not earlier than the start date. |
| `day_count` | `act_365_fixed` \| `act_360` \| `act_act_isda` \| `thirty_360` \| `thirty_e_360` | yes |  | Day-count convention. |

## `dates.schedule`

**Schedule of accrual periods** · method version 1 · status preview · tool `fairmark_dates_schedule`

Start and end dates of n contiguous accrual periods from a start date, each from and including its start date to but excluding its end date (2006 ISDA Definitions): the end date is the first day of the next period. Period length as a frequency (`monthly` 1 month, `bimonthly` 2, `quarterly` 3, `four_monthly` 4, `semi_annual` 6, `annual` 12) or as `period_months`; unadjusted dates with the end-of-month rule; optional year fractions under a day count.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `start_date` | string | yes |  | Start date of the first period (ISO 8601). Each period runs from and including its start date to but excluding its end date, [start, end); the end date of a period is the start date of the next one. |
| `frequency` |  | no |  | Period length as a named frequency: `monthly` (1 month per period, 12 a year), `bimonthly` (2 months, every two months, 6 a year), `quarterly` (3 months, 4 a year), `four_monthly` (4 months, 3 a year), `semi_annual` (6 months, 2 a year) or `annual` (12 months, 1 a year). Give exactly one of `frequency` and `period_months`. |
| `period_months` | integer \| null | no |  | Period length as a positive whole number of months per period (not periods a year), for tenors with or without a name: 1 = `monthly`, 2 = `bimonthly`, 3 = `quarterly`, 4 = `four_monthly`, 6 = `semi_annual`, 12 = `annual`, and any other such as 5, 18 or 24. Give exactly one of `frequency` and `period_months`. |
| `number_of_periods` | integer | yes |  | Number of periods, from 1 to 10000. |
| `day_count` |  | no |  | Day count for the year fraction of each period, measured on [start, end). Optional: without it no year fraction is computed (none is assumed). |

## `series.project`

**Value series projected on a timeline** · method version 1 · status preview · tool `fairmark_series_project`

Values of periods 1 to n grown from a base value period by period, V_k = V_(k−1) × (1 + g_k), with a constant, linear or per-period growth rule; annual rates converted to the period length by a stated basis (compound or proportional). The timeline is a number of periods or a `dates.schedule` definition, whose periods run from and including the start date to but excluding the end date; dated values feed `tvm.xnpv`.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `base_value` | decimal | yes |  | Base value V_0, in the units of the series (currency units for revenues or flows); may be negative. |
| `base_period` | `period_0` \| `period_1` | yes |  | `period_0` (the base value is before period 1, V_1 = V_0 × (1 + g_1)) or `period_1` (the base value is the value of period 1, V_1 = V_0). Required, no default. |
| `growth` |  | yes |  | Growth rule, externally tagged: `constant`, `linear` or `per_period`. |
| `growth_basis` |  | no |  | How the growth rates are read: `per_period`, `annual_compound` or `annual_simple`. Required when the timeline has a period length other than 12 months; may be omitted with 12-month periods (the three bases coincide) or without a period length (rates per period). The annual bases need a period length that divides 12 or is a multiple of 12. |
| `timeline` |  | yes |  | The periods: `periods` (a number of periods) or `schedule` (dated periods, built as by `dates.schedule`). |
| `timing` |  | no |  | With a `schedule` timeline only, and then required: `end_of_period` (each value dated at the end date of its period, the first day of the next period) or `beginning_of_period` (at its start date). |

## `rates.convert`

**Rate conversion between compounding conventions** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_rates_convert`

Equivalent annual rate under another compounding (annual, semi-annual, four-monthly, quarterly, bimonthly, monthly, continuous).

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rate` | decimal | yes |  | Annual rate as a decimal fraction (0.12 = 12% a year), quoted with `from` compounding. |
| `from` | `annual` \| `semi_annual` \| `quarterly` \| `monthly` \| `continuous` \| `bimonthly` \| `four_monthly` | yes |  | Compounding of the given rate. |
| `to` | `annual` \| `semi_annual` \| `quarterly` \| `monthly` \| `continuous` \| `bimonthly` \| `four_monthly` | yes |  | Compounding of the equivalent rate to return. |

## `rates.real_nominal`

**Real and nominal rates (Fisher)** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_rates_real_nominal`

Converts a nominal rate to a real rate, or the reverse, with the exact Fisher relation.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rate` | decimal | yes |  | Rate to convert, decimal fraction per period (0.08 = 8%). |
| `inflation` | decimal | yes |  | Inflation over the same period, decimal fraction (0.03 = 3%). |
| `direction` | `to_real` \| `to_nominal` | yes |  | `to_real` or `to_nominal`. |

## `tvm.npv`

**Net present value** · method version 2 · status available · tool `fairmark_tvm_npv`

Net present value of a cash flow series; the first flow is at t = 0.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rate` | decimal | yes |  | Discount rate per period as a decimal fraction (0.10 = 10%). |
| `cash_flows` | list of decimal | yes |  | Cash flows; the first one occurs at t = 0 (no discounting). |

## `tvm.present_value`

**Present value with a constant or time-varying rate** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_tvm_present_value`

Present value of periodic flows for periods 1..n with one rate or one rate per period, at end, mid or beginning of period. Returns every discount factor.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cash_flows` | list of decimal | yes |  | Cash flows of periods 1, 2, ..., n, in currency units. |
| `rate` | decimal | no |  | One discount rate for every period, decimal fraction per period. Give exactly one of `rate` and `period_rates`. |
| `period_rates` | array \| null | no |  | One discount rate per period (forward period rates, decimal fractions), exactly one per cash flow. |
| `timing` | `end_of_period` \| `mid_period` \| `beginning_of_period` | yes |  | When flows occur within each period. |

## `tvm.xnpv`

**Net present value of dated cash flows (XNPV)** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_tvm_xnpv`

Present value of dated flows at a valuation date, with explicit day count and compounding (defaults as in ECMA-376 XNPV).

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rate` | decimal | yes |  | Annual discount rate, decimal fraction (0.09 = 9%), quoted with `compounding`. |
| `cash_flows` | list of object | yes |  | Dated cash flows, in any order. |
| `valuation_date` |  | no |  | Date at which the value is computed. Default: the earliest flow date (ECMA-376 XNPV). |
| `day_count` |  | no |  | Day count for the time between dates. Default: `act_365_fixed` (ECMA-376 XNPV). |
| `compounding` |  | no |  | Compounding of `rate`. Default: `annual` (ECMA-376 XNPV). |

## `tvm.irr`

**Internal rate of return** · method version 3 · status available · tool `fairmark_tvm_irr`

Rate at which the NPV of a periodic cash flow series is zero, solved deterministically; refuses inputs with more than one IRR.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cash_flows` | list of decimal | yes |  | Cash flows; the first one occurs at t = 0. Needs at least one sign change. |
| `guess` | decimal | no |  | Starting point for Newton's method, decimal fraction per period, greater than -1 (-100%). Default: 0.10. |

## `tvm.xirr`

**Internal rate of return of dated cash flows (XIRR)** · method version 2 · status available · tool `fairmark_tvm_xirr`

Annual rate at which the XNPV of dated flows is zero, solved deterministically; refuses inputs with more than one rate.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cash_flows` | list of object | yes |  | Dated cash flows, in any order; at least one positive and one negative amount. |
| `day_count` |  | no |  | Day count for the time between dates. Default: `act_365_fixed` (ECMA-376 XIRR). |
| `compounding` |  | no |  | Compounding of the returned rate. Default: `annual` (ECMA-376 XIRR). |
| `guess` | decimal | no |  | Starting point for Newton's method, annual decimal fraction in the compounding of the result, greater than -m, with m the compounding periods a year (-1 annual, -2 semi-annual, -3 four-monthly, -4 quarterly, -6 bimonthly, -12 monthly; no bound for continuous). Default: 0.10 (ECMA-376 XIRR). |

## `tvm.mirr`

**Modified internal rate of return (MIRR)** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_tvm_mirr`

Rate of return with negative flows financed at a finance rate and positive flows reinvested at a reinvestment rate (ECMA-376 MIRR).

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cash_flows` | list of decimal | yes |  | Periodic cash flows; the first one occurs at t = 0. At least one positive and one negative. |
| `finance_rate` | decimal | yes |  | Rate paid on the money invested (applied to negative flows), decimal fraction per period. |
| `reinvest_rate` | decimal | yes |  | Rate earned on reinvested positive flows, decimal fraction per period. |

**Perpetuity (level or growing)** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_tvm_perpetuity`

Present value of a level or growing perpetuity (Gordon), ordinary or due.

## `tvm.future_value`

**Future value of a present amount and level payments** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_tvm_future_value`

Value at the end of n periods of a present amount and a level series of payments, ordinary or due, at a rate per period.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `present_value` | decimal | no |  | Amount at t = 0, in currency units, accumulated to t = n. Default: 0. Give at least one of `present_value` and `payment`. |
| `payment` | decimal | no |  | Level payment of every period, in currency units. Default: 0. An amount of the same sign as the present value accumulates in the same direction; a negative amount is a withdrawal. |
| `rate` | decimal | yes |  | Rate per period, decimal fraction (0.01 = 1% per period). No annual-rate conversion: for an annual rate, convert it first (`rates.convert`) and divide by the periods per year. |
| `periods` | integer | yes |  | Number of periods, from 1 to 10000. |
| `timing` | `ordinary` \| `due` | yes |  | `ordinary` (payments at the end of each period) or `due` (at the beginning). |

## `loans.instalment`

**Loan instalment (constant instalment, optional balloon)** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_loans_instalment`

Constant instalment of a loan from its principal, rate, number of instalments and timing, with an optional balloon amount and an explicit rounding.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `principal` | decimal | yes |  | Amount borrowed, in currency units, greater than zero. |
| `rate` | decimal | no |  | Annual borrowing rate, decimal fraction (0.05 = 5% a year), quoted with `compounding`. Rate form (a): give it with `compounding` and `payment_frequency`, or give `periodic_rate` instead. |
| `compounding` |  | no |  | Compounding of `rate` (form a); required with `rate`, no default. |
| `payment_frequency` |  | no |  | Instalments per year (form a): `annual`, `semi_annual`, `four_monthly` (3 a year), `quarterly`, `bimonthly` (every two months, 6 a year) or `monthly`. |
| `periodic_rate` | decimal | no |  | Rate per payment period, decimal fraction (form b), greater than -1; instead of `rate`, `compounding` and `payment_frequency`. |
| `number_of_instalments` | integer | yes |  | Number of instalments, from 1 to 10000. |
| `timing` | `ordinary` \| `due` | yes |  | `ordinary` (in arrears: instalment k at the end of period k) or `due` (in advance: at the beginning of period k). |
| `balloon_amount` | decimal | no |  | Amount repaid at the end of the last period on top of the last instalment, in currency units, at least 0 and lower than the principal. Default: 0. |
| `rounding` |  | no |  | Rounding of the instalment. Default: none (no rounding). |

## `loans.number_of_instalments`

**Number of instalments of a loan** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_loans_number_of_instalments`

Number of instalments needed to repay a loan with a given instalment, the exact number of periods and the final instalment.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `principal` | decimal | yes |  | Amount borrowed, in currency units, greater than zero. |
| `rate` | decimal | no |  | Annual borrowing rate, decimal fraction (0.05 = 5% a year), quoted with `compounding`. Rate form (a): give it with `compounding` and `payment_frequency`, or give `periodic_rate` instead. |
| `compounding` |  | no |  | Compounding of `rate` (form a); required with `rate`, no default. |
| `payment_frequency` |  | no |  | Instalments per year (form a): `annual`, `semi_annual`, `four_monthly` (3 a year), `quarterly`, `bimonthly` (every two months, 6 a year) or `monthly`. |
| `periodic_rate` | decimal | no |  | Rate per payment period, decimal fraction (form b), greater than -1; instead of `rate`, `compounding` and `payment_frequency`. |
| `instalment` | decimal | yes |  | Constant instalment, in currency units; it must exceed the interest of the first period. |
| `timing` | `ordinary` \| `due` | yes |  | `ordinary` (in arrears: instalment k at the end of period k) or `due` (in advance: at the beginning of period k). |

## `loans.amortisation_schedule`

**Amortisation schedule (French, constant principal, bullet)** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_loans_amortisation_schedule`

Period-by-period schedule of a loan with instalment, interest portion, principal portion and outstanding balance; French, fixed amortisation schedule or bullet, with an optional grace period, balloon amount and rounding.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `principal` | decimal | yes |  | Amount borrowed, in currency units, greater than zero. |
| `rate` | decimal | no |  | Annual borrowing rate, decimal fraction (0.05 = 5% a year), quoted with `compounding`. Rate form (a): give it with `compounding` and `payment_frequency`, or give `periodic_rate` instead. |
| `compounding` |  | no |  | Compounding of `rate` (form a); required with `rate`, no default. |
| `payment_frequency` |  | no |  | Instalments per year (form a): `annual`, `semi_annual`, `four_monthly` (3 a year), `quarterly`, `bimonthly` (every two months, 6 a year) or `monthly`. |
| `periodic_rate` | decimal | no |  | Rate per payment period, decimal fraction (form b), greater than -1; instead of `rate`, `compounding` and `payment_frequency`. |
| `number_of_instalments` | integer | yes |  | Number of instalments over the full term, grace periods included, from 1 to 10000. |
| `timing` | `ordinary` \| `due` | yes |  | `ordinary` (in arrears: instalment k at the end of period k, time k). Version 1 accepts only `ordinary`; `due` is refused with `FM-E001`. |
| `amortisation_type` | `french` \| `fixed_amortisation_schedule` \| `bullet` | yes |  | `french` (constant instalment), `fixed_amortisation_schedule` (constant principal portion) or `bullet` (principal repaid with the last instalment). |
| `principal_grace_periods` | integer \| null | no |  | Number of interest-only periods at the start, lower than `number_of_instalments`. Default: 0. Not accepted with `bullet`. |
| `balloon_amount` | decimal | no |  | Principal repaid with the last instalment on top of the amortised amount, in currency units, at least 0 and lower than the principal. Default: 0. Not accepted with `bullet`. |
| `rounding` |  | no |  | Rounding of the amount the schedule type keeps constant: the instalment (`french`) or the principal portion (`fixed_amortisation_schedule`). Interest is never rounded. Default: none (no rounding). |

## `coc.cost_of_equity`

**Cost of equity (CAPM with explicit premia)** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_coc_cost_of_equity`

Cost of equity from risk-free rate, levered or relevered beta and equity risk premium, plus optional country, size and specific premia, each reported.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `risk_free_rate` | decimal | yes |  | Risk-free rate, annual decimal fraction. |
| `equity_risk_premium` | decimal | yes |  | Equity risk premium of the market, annual decimal fraction. |
| `levered_beta` | decimal | no |  | Levered beta, dimensionless. Give exactly one of `levered_beta` and `relever`. |
| `relever` |  | no |  | Unlevered beta and target structure to relever. Give exactly one of `levered_beta` and `relever`. |
| `country_risk_premium` | decimal | no |  | Country risk premium, annual decimal fraction, not negative. Default: 0. |
| `country_exposure` | decimal | no |  | Exposure of the company to the country risk (lambda), dimensionless, not negative. Default: 1. |
| `size_premium` | decimal | no |  | Size premium, annual decimal fraction. Default: 0. |
| `specific_risk_premium` | decimal | no |  | Company-specific risk premium, annual decimal fraction. Default: 0. When not zero, `specific_risk_justification` is required. |
| `specific_risk_justification` | string \| null | no |  | Written reason for the specific risk premium, echoed in the audit trail. |

## `coc.beta_relever`

**Beta unlevering and relevering** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_coc_beta_relever`

Converts an unlevered beta to a levered beta at a target D/E, or the reverse, with the Hamada or Harris-Pringle formula and an optional debt beta.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `beta` | decimal | yes |  | Beta to convert (unlevered for `relever`, levered for `unlever`), dimensionless. |
| `direction` | `relever` \| `unlever` | yes |  | `relever` or `unlever`. |
| `debt_to_equity` | decimal | yes |  | Debt-to-equity ratio D/E, decimal (0.5 = debt equal to half of equity), not negative. |
| `tax_rate` | decimal | yes |  | Tax rate of the tax shield, decimal fraction from 0 to below 1. |
| `formula` | `hamada` \| `harris_pringle` | yes |  | `hamada` or `harris_pringle`. |
| `debt_beta` | decimal | no |  | Beta of debt, dimensionless. Default: 0 (risk-free debt). |

## `coc.beta_peers`

**Beta from comparable companies** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_coc_beta_peers`

Unlevers the betas of comparable companies, takes the mean or median and relevers it to the target capital structure.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `peers` | list of object | yes |  | Comparable companies, at least one. |
| `formula` | `hamada` \| `harris_pringle` | yes |  | `hamada` or `harris_pringle`, used to unlever and to relever. |
| `statistic` | `mean` \| `median` | yes |  | `mean` or `median` of the unlevered betas. |
| `target_debt_to_equity` | decimal | yes |  | Target debt-to-equity ratio D/E of the company being valued, decimal, not negative. |
| `target_tax_rate` | decimal | yes |  | Tax rate of the company being valued, decimal fraction from 0 to below 1. |
| `debt_beta` | decimal | no |  | Beta of debt, dimensionless, for peers and target. Default: 0 (risk-free debt). |

## `tv.gordon`

**Terminal value, stable growth (Gordon)** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_tv_gordon`

Terminal value at the horizon N of a flow growing at g forever, CF_{N+1} / (r − g), from the next flow or the last flow grown by g; not discounted.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rate` | decimal | yes |  | Discount rate of the terminal phase, decimal fraction per period; must exceed `growth`. It may differ from the rate of the explicit phase. |
| `growth` | decimal | yes |  | Perpetual growth of the flow, decimal fraction per period, greater than -1 and below `rate`. |
| `next_flow` | decimal | no |  | Flow of the first period after the horizon, CF_{N+1}, in currency units (for example a normalised flow). Give this or `last_flow`, not both. |
| `last_flow` | decimal | no |  | Flow of the last explicit period, CF_N, in currency units; grown by `growth` to CF_{N+1}. Give this or `next_flow`, not both. |
| `growth_cap` | decimal | no |  | Upper bound for the perpetual growth, decimal fraction per period (for example the risk-free rate or the nominal growth of the economy). Default: none, reported as absent. A growth above the cap is reported, not refused. |

## `tv.value_driver`

**Terminal value, value driver (growth from reinvestment)** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_tv_value_driver`

Terminal value at the horizon N with growth earned by reinvesting g / RONIC of NOPAT: NOPAT_{N+1} × (1 − g / RONIC) / (r − g); reports the reinvestment rate and whether growth creates value.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `nopat_next` | decimal | yes |  | Net operating profit after tax of the first period after the horizon, NOPAT_{N+1}, in currency units. |
| `growth` | decimal | yes |  | Perpetual growth, decimal fraction per period, greater than -1 and below `rate`. |
| `ronic` | decimal | yes |  | Return on new invested capital (RONIC), decimal fraction per period, greater than 0. |
| `rate` | decimal | yes |  | Discount rate of the terminal phase, decimal fraction per period; must exceed `growth`. |
| `growth_cap` | decimal | no |  | Upper bound for the perpetual growth, decimal fraction per period. Default: none, reported as absent. A growth above the cap is reported, not refused. |

## `tv.h_model`

**Terminal value, H-model (declining growth)** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_tv_h_model`

Terminal value at the horizon N when growth declines linearly from g_s to g_l over 2H periods: CF_N × [(1 + g_l) + H × (g_s − g_l)] / (r − g_l), an approximation.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `last_flow` | decimal | yes |  | Flow of the last explicit period, CF_N, in currency units. |
| `short_term_growth` | decimal | yes |  | Growth at the start of the decline, g_s, decimal fraction per period, greater than -1. |
| `long_term_growth` | decimal | yes |  | Stable growth reached after 2H periods and kept forever, g_l, decimal fraction per period, greater than -1 and below `rate`. |
| `half_life` | decimal | yes |  | Half-life H, in periods: the decline from g_s to g_l lasts 2H periods. Zero or positive; may be fractional. |
| `rate` | decimal | yes |  | Discount rate of the terminal phase, decimal fraction per period; must exceed `long_term_growth`. |
| `growth_cap` | decimal | no |  | Upper bound for the long-term growth, decimal fraction per period. Default: none, reported as absent. A growth above the cap is reported, not refused. |

## `tv.exit_multiple`

**Terminal value, exit multiple** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_tv_exit_multiple`

Terminal value at the horizon N as a multiple of EBITDA, EBIT, revenue (enterprise basis), earnings or book value of equity (equity basis); with a rate and the next flow, reports the implied perpetual growth.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `multiple` | decimal | yes |  | The multiple, a pure number greater than 0 (for example 8 for 8 × EBITDA). |
| `metric` | `ebitda` \| `ebit` \| `revenue` \| `earnings` \| `book_value` | yes |  | `ebitda`, `ebit`, `revenue` (enterprise basis), `earnings` or `book_value` (equity basis). |
| `metric_value` | decimal | yes |  | The metric at the horizon N, in currency units, greater than 0. |
| `rate` | decimal | no |  | Discount rate of the terminal phase, decimal fraction per period, on the basis of the metric (WACC for enterprise, cost of equity for equity). Optional, with `next_flow`: both or neither. Used only for the implied growth. |
| `next_flow` | decimal | no |  | Flow at N + 1 on the basis of the metric (FCFF for enterprise, FCFE for equity), in currency units. Optional, with `rate`: both or neither. |
| `growth_cap` | decimal | no |  | Upper bound for the implied growth, decimal fraction per period. Default: none, reported as absent. Needs `rate` and `next_flow`. Exceeding it is reported, not refused. |

## `tv.limited_horizon`

**Terminal value, finite horizon** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_tv_limited_horizon`

Terminal value at the horizon N of a flow lasting n more periods, constant or growing, plus a residual value at N + n (Italian practice); reuses the annuity factor of tvm.annuity.

| `flow` | decimal | yes |  | First flow after the horizon, at the end of period N + 1, in currency units. |
| `rate` | decimal | yes |  | Discount rate of the terminal phase, decimal fraction per period, greater than -1. |
| `periods` | integer | yes |  | Number of further periods n during which the flow lasts, from 1 to 10000. |
| `growth` | decimal | no |  | Growth of the flow per period, decimal fraction, greater than -1. Default: 0 (constant flow). |
| `residual_value` | decimal | no |  | Residual value at the end of period N + n, in currency units. Default: 0. |
| `growth_cap` | decimal | no |  | Upper bound for the growth, decimal fraction per period. Default: none, reported as absent. A growth above the cap is reported, not refused. |

## `tv.normalised_income`

**Terminal value, capitalised normalised income** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_tv_normalised_income`

| `income` | decimal | yes |  | Normalised income R of the first period after the horizon, in currency units. |

| `growth_cap` | decimal | no |  | Upper bound for the growth, decimal fraction per period. Default: none, reported as absent. A growth above the cap is reported, not refused. |

## `tv.compare`

**Terminal value, comparison of techniques** · method version 2 · status available · tool `fairmark_tv_compare`

Runs several terminal value techniques on one rate, growth cap and basis and returns each terminal value at the horizon N with its implied assumptions, side by side.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rate` | decimal | yes |  | Discount rate of the terminal phase, decimal fraction per period, shared by every technique that uses a discount rate. |
| `basis` | `enterprise` \| `equity` | yes |  | `enterprise` or `equity`: the basis of every terminal value compared. An exit multiple of the other basis is refused. |
| `growth_cap` | decimal | no |  | Upper bound for the perpetual growth, decimal fraction per period, shared by every growth-based technique. Default: none, reported as absent. |
| `techniques` | list of  | yes |  | Techniques to run, at least one, each an object with exactly one key, the method id: `{"tv.<name>": {terms}}`. The same technique may appear in more than one entry; a key repeated within one entry is refused. |

## `dcf.fcff`

**DCF — unlevered free cash flow** · method version 3 · status preview · tool `fairmark_dcf_fcff`

Value of operations, enterprise value and equity value from FCFF discounted at the WACC over one to three explicit stages (given flows, constant growth, linear decline of growth) and a terminal value by a tv.* technique on the enterprise basis (stable growth, H-model, value driver, exit multiple, finite horizon, normalised income, liquidation), given as an amount, or none. The minimal input is a list of FCFF and one WACC; the defaults applied are reported. Returns every period and step for audit.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stages` | list of object | yes |  | One to three explicit stages, in order; the explicit horizon N is the sum of their periods. Each stage is `{"periods", "projection", ...}` with the fields of its projection; a stage of given FCFF can be just `{"flows": [...]}` (projection `given` and periods the number of flows, by default). |
| `base_flow` | decimal | no |  | FCFF of the base period CF_0, in currency units: required when the first stage is `constant_growth` or `linear_decline`, refused when it is `given`. |
| `notional_tax_rate` | decimal | no |  | For stages with `lines`: tax rate applied to EBIT, decimal fraction from 0 to below 1 (0.24 = 24%). Give this, or `operating_taxes` in every line, not both; refused when no stage has `lines`. Default: none. |
| `negative_ebit` |  | no |  | For stages with `lines` and `notional_tax_rate`: treatment of a negative EBIT, `credit` (taxes = rate × EBIT) or `zero` (no tax); required with `notional_tax_rate`, no default. |
| `cash_flow_terms` | `nominal` \| `real` | no |  | `nominal` or `real`: the terms of every amount and growth rate of the input. Default: `nominal`, reported. |
| `discount_rate_terms` | `nominal` \| `real` | no |  | `nominal` or `real`: the terms of the discount rates. When they differ from `cash_flow_terms`, expected inflation is required (`inflation`, or `inflation_per_period` with `terminal_inflation`) and every rate is converted to the terms of the cash flows; the cash flows are never converted. Default: `nominal`, reported. |
| `inflation` | decimal | no |  | Expected inflation, decimal fraction per period (0.02 = 2%), greater than -1, for every explicit period and for the terminal phase. Give this or `inflation_per_period`, or neither. With different terms it converts the discount rates by the exact Fisher relation; with equal terms it only restates the perpetual growth in the other terms. Default: none. |
| `inflation_per_period` | array \| null | no |  | Expected inflation per period of the explicit horizon, decimal fractions, exactly N of them, each greater than -1; requires `terminal_inflation`. Give this or `inflation`, not both. Default: none. |
| `terminal_inflation` | decimal | no |  | Expected inflation of the terminal phase, decimal fraction per period, greater than -1; required with `inflation_per_period` when the terminal value uses a terminal rate, refused otherwise. |
| `wacc` | decimal | no |  | One WACC for every period and for the terminal value, decimal fraction per period (0.09 = 9%), greater than -1. Give this or `wacc_per_period`, not both. |
| `wacc_per_period` | array \| null | no |  | One WACC per period of the explicit horizon, decimal fractions, exactly N of them, each greater than -1; requires `terminal_wacc`. Give this or `wacc`, not both. |
| `terminal_wacc` | decimal | no |  | WACC of the terminal phase, decimal fraction per period, greater than -1; required with `wacc_per_period`, refused with `wacc`. |
| `timing` | `end_of_period` \| `mid_period` | no |  | `end_of_period` (flow k at t = k) or `mid_period` (t = k − 0.5). Default: `end_of_period`, reported. |
| `terminal_discount_time` |  | no |  | With `mid_period` timing and a terminal value to discount, required: `horizon` (terminal value at t = N) or `mid_period` (t = N − 0.5). Refused with `end_of_period` and with no terminal value. |
| `terminal` | object | no |  | The terminal option, an object with exactly one key: a technique by its method id, for example `{"tv.gordon": {"growth", "first_flow", ...}}` (`tv.gordon`, `tv.h_model`, `tv.value_driver`, `tv.exit_multiple`, `tv.limited_horizon`, `tv.normalised_income` or `tv.liquidation`, on the enterprise basis); `{"given": {"value": ...}}`, a terminal value at N given by the analyst (the value of operations at N); or `{"none": {}}`, no terminal value. Default: `none`, the value covers the given flows only, reported with a warning. |
| `net_financial_position` |  | no |  | Net financial position at the valuation date (SPEC-0007): gross debt − cash + signed other items, positive for net debt, subtracted from enterprise value. Default: none, reported. |
| `non_operating_assets` | list of object | no |  | Non-operating assets at the valuation date, each a label and a value in currency units (zero or more), added to the value of operations. Default: none, reported. |
| `debt_like_items` | list of object | no |  | Debt-like items (debt equivalents) at the valuation date, for example unfunded pension obligations or provisions, each a label, a value in currency units (zero or more) and its measurement basis, subtracted from enterprise value. Do not repeat an item already among the `other_items` of the net financial position. Default: none, reported. |
| `non_controlling_interests` | list of object | no |  | Non-controlling interests (minority interests) at the valuation date, each a label, a value in currency units (zero or more) and its measurement basis (for example `book_value` or `fair_value`), subtracted from enterprise value. Default: none, reported. |

## `dcf.fcfe`

**DCF — free cash flow to equity** · method version 1 · status preview · tool `fairmark_dcf_fcfe`

Equity value from FCFE discounted at the cost of equity over one to three explicit stages (given flows or flows built up from line items with interest and net borrowing, constant growth, linear decline of growth) and a terminal value by a tv.* technique on the equity basis, plus non-operating assets, minus debt-like items and non-controlling interests; no net financial position, debt is in the flows. The terminal value may also be given as an amount, or none. The minimal input is a list of FCFE and one cost of equity; the defaults applied are reported. Returns every period and step for audit.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stages` | list of object | yes |  | One to three explicit stages of free cash flows to equity (FCFE), in order; the explicit horizon N is the sum of their periods. Each stage is `{"periods", "projection", ...}` with the fields of its projection; a `given` stage takes the FCFE as amounts (`flows`) or builds them up from line items with `interest_expense` and `net_borrowing` in every line (`lines`); a stage of given FCFE can be just `{"flows": [...]}` (projection `given` and periods the number of flows, by default). |
| `base_flow` | decimal | no |  | FCFE of the base period CF_0, in currency units: required when the first stage is `constant_growth` or `linear_decline`, refused when it is `given`. |
| `notional_tax_rate` | decimal | no |  | For stages with `lines`: tax rate applied to EBIT, decimal fraction from 0 to below 1 (0.24 = 24%), also the rate of the interest tax shield. Give this, or `operating_taxes` in every line, not both; refused when no stage has `lines`. Default: none. |
| `negative_ebit` |  | no |  | For stages with `lines` and `notional_tax_rate`: treatment of a negative EBIT, `credit` (taxes = rate × EBIT) or `zero` (no tax; the interest tax shield is limited to the taxable income, rate × min(interest, max(EBIT, 0)), Decision 22); required with `notional_tax_rate`, no default. |
| `interest_tax_rate` | decimal | no |  | For stages with `lines` and `operating_taxes`: the tax rate t of the interest tax shield, interest × (1 − t), decimal fraction from 0 to below 1; required in that case, refused otherwise. Default: none. |
| `cash_flow_terms` | `nominal` \| `real` | no |  | `nominal` or `real`: the terms of every amount and growth rate of the input. Default: `nominal`, reported. |
| `discount_rate_terms` | `nominal` \| `real` | no |  | `nominal` or `real`: the terms of the discount rates. When they differ from `cash_flow_terms`, expected inflation is required (`inflation`, or `inflation_per_period` with `terminal_inflation`) and every rate is converted to the terms of the cash flows; the cash flows are never converted. Default: `nominal`, reported. |
| `inflation` | decimal | no |  | Expected inflation, decimal fraction per period (0.02 = 2%), greater than -1, for every explicit period and for the terminal phase. Give this or `inflation_per_period`, or neither. With different terms it converts the discount rates by the exact Fisher relation; with equal terms it only restates the perpetual growth in the other terms. Default: none. |
| `inflation_per_period` | array \| null | no |  | Expected inflation per period of the explicit horizon, decimal fractions, exactly N of them, each greater than -1; requires `terminal_inflation`. Give this or `inflation`, not both. Default: none. |
| `terminal_inflation` | decimal | no |  | Expected inflation of the terminal phase, decimal fraction per period, greater than -1; required with `inflation_per_period` when the terminal value uses a terminal rate, refused otherwise. |
| `cost_of_equity` | decimal | no |  | One cost of equity for every period and for the terminal value, decimal fraction per period (0.11 = 11%), greater than -1. Give this or `cost_of_equity_per_period`, not both. |
| `cost_of_equity_per_period` | array \| null | no |  | One cost of equity per period of the explicit horizon, decimal fractions, exactly N of them, each greater than -1; requires `terminal_cost_of_equity`. Give this or `cost_of_equity`, not both. |
| `terminal_cost_of_equity` | decimal | no |  | Cost of equity of the terminal phase, decimal fraction per period, greater than -1; required with `cost_of_equity_per_period`, refused with `cost_of_equity`. |
| `timing` | `end_of_period` \| `mid_period` | no |  | `end_of_period` (flow k at t = k) or `mid_period` (t = k − 0.5). Default: `end_of_period`, reported. |
| `terminal_discount_time` |  | no |  | With `mid_period` timing and a terminal value to discount, required: `horizon` (terminal value at t = N) or `mid_period` (t = N − 0.5). Refused with `end_of_period` and with no terminal value. |
| `terminal` | object | no |  | The terminal option on the equity basis, an object with exactly one key: a technique by its method id, for example `{"tv.gordon": {"growth", "first_flow", ...}}` (`tv.gordon`, `tv.h_model` or `tv.limited_horizon` on the FCFE, `tv.exit_multiple` on `earnings` (P/E) or `book_value` (P/BV), `tv.normalised_income` or `tv.liquidation` declared on the `equity` basis; `tv.value_driver` is refused: its NOPAT and RONIC are firm-level quantities, SPEC-0001 Decision 23); `{"given": {"value": ...}}`, a terminal value at N given by the analyst (the equity value at N); or `{"none": {}}`, no terminal value. Default: `none`, the value covers the given flows only, reported with a warning. |
| `net_financial_position` |  | no |  | Not used on the equity basis and refused (`FM-E019`): debt is already in the FCFE, through interest and net borrowing, so the net financial position is not subtracted. Cash that the FCFE does not reflect goes in `non_operating_assets`. Accepted by the schema only so that the refusal names the fix. |
| `non_operating_assets` | list of object | no |  | Non-operating assets at the valuation date, each a label and a value in currency units (zero or more), added to the present value of the FCFE and of the terminal value: for example cash not needed for operations whose interest income is not in the FCFE, or an investment property. Default: none, reported. |
| `debt_like_items` | list of object | no |  | Debt-like items (debt equivalents) at the valuation date whose cash flows are not in the FCFE, for example unfunded pension obligations, each a label, a value in currency units (zero or more) and its measurement basis; subtracted. Default: none, reported. |
| `non_controlling_interests` | list of object | no |  | Non-controlling interests (minority interests) at the valuation date, when the FCFE are those of the consolidated group, each a label, a value in currency units (zero or more) and its measurement basis; subtracted. Default: none, reported. |

## `dcf.free_cash_flows`

**Free cash flow build-up (FCFF and FCFE)** · method version 2 · status preview · tool `fairmark_dcf_free_cash_flows`

FCFF per period from EBIT, taxes on EBIT (a rate or amounts), depreciation and amortisation, capital expenditure, change in net working capital and labelled adjustments; FCFE when interest expense and net borrowing are given. Not discounted.

## `analysis.goal_seek`

**Goal seek** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_analysis_goal_seek`

Value of one decimal input of any method at which one of its outputs equals a target, found with Brent's method in an explicit bracket; every evaluation is reported.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | string | yes |  | Id of the method to evaluate, for example `dcf.fcff`. Analysis methods are not accepted. |
| `base_input` | object | yes |  | Input of that method, complete, including the variable at any starting value. |
| `variable` | string | yes |  | RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the decimal input to solve for, for example `/discount_rate`. |
| `output` | string | yes |  | RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the decimal output of the method, in its `value`, for example `/enterprise_value`. |
| `target` | decimal | yes |  | Value the output must reach, in the output's units. |
| `bracket` | list of decimal | yes |  | `[low, high]`, low < high: the variable is searched in this interval, and the output minus the target must change sign between its ends (or meet the tolerance at one end). |
| `tolerance` | decimal | no | `"0.000000001"` | Absolute tolerance on the output, in the output's units, greater than 0. Default: 0.000000001. |
| `max_iterations` | integer | no | `100` | Largest number of evaluations after the two bracket ends, from 1 to 1000. Default: 100. |

| `method` | string | yes |  | Id of the method to evaluate, for example `dcf.fcff`. Analysis methods are not accepted. |
| `base_input` | object | yes |  | Input of that method, complete: the base case. |
| `output` | string | yes |  | RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the decimal output reported in each cell, in the `value` of the inner result, for example `/enterprise_value`. |
| `rows` | object | yes |  | The variable that changes along the rows, and its values. |
| `columns` |  | no |  | Optional second variable, along the columns, different from the row variable. Absent: a one-way table (one column). |

## `analysis.scenarios`

**Scenario analysis** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_analysis_scenarios`

Outputs of any method under named sets of input changes, with deltas and relative deltas against the base case; a scenario the method refuses is recorded.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | string | yes |  | Id of the method to evaluate, for example `dcf.fcff`. Analysis methods are not accepted. |
| `base_input` | object | yes |  | Input of that method, complete: the base case. |
| `outputs` | list of string | yes |  | RFC 6901 JSON Pointers to the decimal outputs to report, in the `value` of the inner result, for example `["/enterprise_value", "/equity_value"]`; at least one, no repeats. |
| `scenarios` | list of object | yes |  | The cases, evaluated in this order; at least one. |

## `analysis.tornado`

**Tornado** · method version 1 · status available · tool `fairmark_analysis_tornado`

Which inputs move one output of any method the most: each input varied alone between explicit low and high values, ranked by the absolute swing of the output.

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | string | yes |  | Id of the method to evaluate, for example `dcf.fcff`. Analysis methods are not accepted. |
| `base_input` | object | yes |  | Input of that method, complete: the base case. Each variable is changed alone, the others keep their base values. |
| `output` | string | yes |  | RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the decimal output to rank, in the `value` of the inner result, for example `/equity_value`. |
| `variables` | list of object | yes |  | The inputs to vary; at least one. |
